correctness.rationale: The quartic defining \(\mathbb F_{81}\) has neither a root nor an irreducible quadratic factor over F_3; each of the 81 centers has exactly 40 distinct nonloop square-adjacencies. At every query the candidate-center mask splits the center set into precisely the two possible traces. Both independently implemented finite enumerations exhaust all 24,040,016 zero-containing six-subsets and find no shattered six-subset, while 587,400 zero-containing five-subsets are shattered. The translation double count \(k f_k=81 h_k\) gives the exact polynomial. No larger support can be shattered since \(2^7>81\). An independent standard-library Python program exhaustively partitions all 82,160 zero-containing four-supports into G-orbits and tests the two nonextendable shattered orbits; the nonpurity conclusion is therefore exact in this finite domain. Limits: no infinite family inference.

value.rationale: The graph is the first natural odd-characteristic quartic-extension Paley example; its order is 81, just above a power-of-two VC threshold. The exact five-level polynomial and three exceptional bad-quartet orbits show sharply how near-universal four-query shattering nevertheless fails to extend to six queries. The two further orbits of maximal four-faces establish a nonpure shattering complex and explicitly identify obstruction geometry. These are intrinsically informative structural invariants of the whole canonical graph, not a tiny arbitrary slice or mere recoding of the order-25 calculation.
